why: Could not refute; all three checks confirm the finding. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window.md yields at line 29, inside the interactive ContextWindow component's EVENTS array for the 'Auto memory (MEMORY.md)' entry: desc: "Claude's notes to itself from previous sessions: build commands it learned, patterns it noticed, mistakes to avoid. The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context." Read the whole line - it is a three-sentence desc field and nothing in it reverses or qualifies the cap. The sibling entry at line 76 ('Keep it under 200 lines') is a tip for project CLAUDE.md, a different event, so no cross-subsystem confusion. (2) CITED CODE: memory-store.ts:8 is exactly `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` - a LINE cap only; there is no byte/KB cap anywhere on the load path (the only byte constants nearby are AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 in memory-cleanup.ts:33, a guard that SKIPS cleanup on large files, and MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES in native-sources.ts, which applies to nested instruction files, not MEMORY.md). materializer.ts:181 is exactly `const content = readFileSync(contentPath);` returning `content.toString('utf-8')` at :186 - a whole-file read with no slice. base-agent.ts:989 has drifted ~12 lines: the actual `const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource);` inside the `for (const layer of runtime.view.memory)` loop is now base-agent.ts:976-977. Line drift only; the substance is present, and AGENTS.md's own trap note says a line number decays while the quoted construct does not. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, and it is the reverse of the usual false positive - here the capped path is the DEAD one. prompts/system.ts:453-455 reads `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`. Only loadMemoryPromptBlock reaches readMemoryFileWithImports -> readMemoryFile(maxLines = 200), so the 200-line cap lives exclusively on the legacy branch. Both live agents pass capabilityContextPinned as `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256), so on any capability turn the capped branch returns '' and memory arrives only through composePinnedCapabilityContext. The repo states this itself in packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts:10-14: 'that block is gated on `capabilityContextPinned`, which is TRUE on every normal Pi turn, so the path they named is dead in production.' memory-store.ts:280-288 agrees in prose: the legacy block 'is only the fallback for turns that run without that runtime.' MEMORY.md genuinely is a capability memory layer - memoryFileRecords is called on join(configDir,'MEMORY.md') (native-sources.ts:909), the session MEMORY.md (:978), .nessy-agent/MEMORY.md (:1027) and the project MEMORY.md (:1092) - so runtime.view.memory is the right subsystem, not a same-named sibling. The one readMemoryFile call inside the capability path (native-sources.ts:427) is used only to scan for @import lines during discovery; it never produces the content that enters context. I also traced downstream: composePinnedCapabilityContext's bodies are consumed at base-agent.ts:889-892 and following with no truncation, so nothing upstream or downstream reinstates a cap. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) - none touch memory load caps. Not a branding, subscription-flow, or gateway product difference either. Caveat on scope, not on truth: this is the same underlying defect already recorded against memory.md, so it should be tracked as a duplicate restatement of that row rather than as an independent second gap.
correctedState: Two separate shortfalls, and the byte cap is missing on BOTH paths. Neither path applies the 25KB cap: no byte/size limit exists anywhere on the memory load path (memory-store.ts:8 defines only MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200; AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 at memory-cleanup.ts:33 is a cleanup skip-guard, not a load cap). The 200-line cap does exist but only on the legacy fallback (loadMemoryPromptBlock -> readMemoryFileWithImports -> readMemoryFile, memory-store.ts:29), which prompts/system.ts:453-455 gates OFF whenever capabilityContextPinned is true - i.e. on every turn with a capability runtime, which is both live agents (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256). On that live path, base-agent.ts:976-977 reads each runtime.view.memory layer through materializer.readText (materializer.ts:181, whole-file readFileSync) and pushes it verbatim into the pinned capability block with neither a line nor a byte cap, so an oversized MEMORY.md enters context in full. Fix belongs at the composePinnedCapabilityContext seam (apply min(200 lines, 25KB) to memory-format layers) rather than in readMemoryFile, since readMemoryFile is already bypassed in production. Track as a duplicate of the memory.md finding; this page only restates it as a context-budget guarantee.
